comparisons.peer_topic: Minimum CET1 Capital Ratio Requirements and Buffers
comparisons.peer_summary: To avoid restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments, the Corporation must meet CET1 capital ratio requirements including buffers and G-SIB surcharges, requiring minimum ratios of 10.0% from Jan 1 to Sep 30, 2024, and 10.7% (Standardized) or 10.0% (Advanced) from Oct 1, 2024. These requirements must be comprised solely of CET1 capital.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC detail their minimum CET1 capital ratio requirements, which include buffers and surcharges, and note the timing of effectiveness changes in late 2024. JPM states its Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement was 12.3% as of December 31, 2024, with an SCB of 3.3% effective until September 2025. BAC specifies that its minimum CET1 capital ratio requirements increased to 10.7% under the Standardized approach effective October 1, 2024, while remaining at 10.0% from January 1 to September 30, 2024. Both companies highlight that these requirements are driven by SCBs and G-SIB surcharges.

sentences.text: The Firm's Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement, including regulatory buffers, was 12.3% as of December 31, 2024.

For the period from January 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024, the Corporation's minimum CET1 capital ratio requirements were 10.0 percent under both the Standardized approach and the Advanced approaches.
Effective October 1, 2024, the Corporation's minimum CET1 requirements were 10.7 percent under the Standardized approach and 10.0 percent under the Advanced approaches.

In order to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers, the Corporation must meet risk-based capital ratio requirements that include a capital conservation buffer of 2.5 percent (under the Advanced approaches only), an SCB (under the Standardized approach only), plus any applicable countercyclical capital buffer and a global systemically important bank (G-SIB) surcharge.

comparisons.peer_summary: Following the 2024 CCAR submission, the FRB increased the SCB from 5.5% to 6.2%, resulting in a Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement of 13.7% for the period from October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025, with DFAST results published in June 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS disclose specific Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirements resulting from the Federal Reserve's stress testing (CCAR) for the relevant 2024/2025 period. JPM reports its requirement was 12.3% as of December 31, 2024, based on an SCB of 3.3%. In contrast, GS reports a higher Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement of 13.7% for the period from October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025, resulting from a larger SCB increase from 5.5% to 6.2% following the 2024 CCAR submission.

sentences.text: The Firm's current SCB requirement is 3.3% and will remain in effect until September 30, 2025.
The Firm's Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement, including regulatory buffers, was 12.3% as of December 31, 2024.

Based on our 2024 CCAR submission, the FRB increased our SCB from 5.5% to 6.2%, resulting in a Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement of 13.7% for the period from October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: Composition of CET1 Capital Buffer Requirement
comparisons.peer_summary: The CET1 capital buffer requirement represents the additional capital needed to avoid restrictions on distributions and discretionary bonuses. Under the Standardized Approach, it is the sum of the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB), G-SIB surcharge, and Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB); under the Advanced Approach, it is the sum of the 2.5% capital conservation buffer, G-SIB surcharge, and CCyB.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and MS explain the composition of the capital buffer requirements applied to their Standardized Approach capital ratios. JPM identifies its current SCB requirement of 3.3% as part of its Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement. MS explicitly defines the capital buffer requirement under the Standardized Approach as the sum of the SCB, G-SIB capital surcharge, and CCyB, which must be maintained above minimum requirements to avoid restrictions on capital distributions.

sentences.text: The Firm's current SCB requirement is 3.3% and will remain in effect until September 30, 2025.
The Firm's Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement, including regulatory buffers, was 12.3% as of December 31, 2024.

The capital buffer requirement represents the amount of CET1 capital we must maintain above the minimum risk-based capital requirements in order to avoid restrictions on our ability to make capital distributions, including the payment of dividends and the repurchase of stock, and to pay discretionary bonuses to executive officers.

Our capital buffer requirement computed under the standardized approaches for calculating credit risk and market RWAs ("Standardized Approach") is equal to the sum of our SCB, G-SIB capital surcharge and CCyB, and our capital buffer requirement computed under the applicable advanced approaches for calculating credit risk, market risk and operational risk RWAs ("Advanced Approach") is equal to our 2.5% capital conservation buffer, G-SIB capital surcharge and CCyB.
